paragraphs: This paper develops a shared framework for optimizing continuous functions with a diminishing-returns structure. It covers both monotone functions, whose value does not decrease as inputs increase, and non-monotone functions. The permitted convex constraint sets differ across these settings, so the framework brings together several related optimization problems without treating their assumptions as interchangeable.

The proposed offline algorithm is of the Frank-Wolfe type. The analysis considers several ways an algorithm might obtain information: it may receive gradients or only function values, and either kind of information may be deterministic or stochastic. For each case, the authors determine how many information requests, called oracle accesses, the method requires.

Across sixteen cases, the framework provides new or improved results in nine, removes expensive projection operations in three, and matches existing leading performance in four. Its stochastic function-value setting also yields the first regret bounds for stochastic DR-submodular functions with bandit feedback. The contribution is therefore both a common analytical approach and specific improvements under different information constraints.
neurips-2023-a-unified-approach-for-maxi.tldr: A unified optimization framework improves guarantees or computational requirements across multiple continuous diminishing-returns settings.

paragraphs: Monte Carlo Tree Search explores possible future decisions through a search tree, and its computational demands depend on the size of that search space. This paper proposes probability tree state abstraction, or PTSA, to make that exploration more efficient. The central idea is to aggregate states in the tree, reducing the space that the search algorithm must handle.

Aggregation introduces a correctness question: simplifying the tree can combine states in ways that create errors. The authors first define a general tree abstraction with a property called path transitivity. They then introduce a probability-based abstraction intended to make fewer aggregation mistakes, and provide theoretical guarantees for transitivity and a bound on aggregation error.

The method is integrated with Sampled MuZero and Gumbel MuZero to test its usefulness within existing search systems. Across the evaluated tasks, the authors report faster training alongside search-space reductions of 10% to 45%. These results support abstraction as a practical way to reduce search demands, while the analysis explicitly addresses errors introduced by the simplification.
neurips-2023-accelerating-monte-carlo-tr.tldr: PTSA aggregates search-tree states with theoretical error guarantees and reduces search space by 10%–45% in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: This paper studies why stochastic gradient descent can converge quickly in heavily overparameterized learning problems. Its focus is the interpolation regime, where models have many more parameters than training samples and can fit the training data. The theoretical question is whether using a sampled gradient must impose a worse iteration requirement than using the deterministic gradient.

The authors propose a regularity condition under which the stochastic method has the same worst-case iteration complexity as the deterministic method. Each stochastic iteration still uses only one sampled gradient or a minibatch. This matters because the earlier guarantees described in the abstract require small stochastic steps, leading to a substantially slower linear convergence rate.

The paper also shows that its condition holds when training sufficiently wide feedforward neural networks with a linear output layer. The result therefore identifies a concrete class of networks where the analysis applies. Its claim is conditional on this regularity and the stated setting: it establishes when fast stochastic convergence is possible, rather than asserting that overparameterization alone always guarantees it.
neurips-2023-aiming-towards-the-minimize.tldr: A regularity condition lets SGD match deterministic gradient descent’s worst-case iteration complexity in certain overparameterized problems.

paragraphs: Risk-averse reinforcement learning seeks policies that perform well while limiting variability in their outcomes. A common approach constrains the variance of the total return, while some methods use the variance of individual rewards as a substitute. This paper examines how these choices can be sensitive to numerical scale and can interfere with learning a useful policy.

The authors propose Gini deviation as an alternative risk measure. They investigate its properties and derive a policy gradient algorithm for minimizing it. The approach changes the quantity used to express risk within the learning procedure, addressing the possibility that the risk objective itself contributes to poor optimization behavior.

Experiments focus on domains where risk aversion has a clear interpretation. In those evaluations, the proposed algorithm mitigates the identified problems and achieves high returns with low risk measured by both variance and Gini deviation, including cases where competing approaches fail to learn a reasonable policy. These findings support the alternative within the tested settings and show that improving the risk formulation can also improve policy learning.
neurips-2023-an-alternative-to-variance-.tldr: A policy gradient method based on Gini deviation mitigates variance-based learning problems in the evaluated risk-averse tasks.

paragraphs: Structural causal models describe systems through variables and the mechanisms connecting them. As a system grows, those relationships can become difficult to analyze or compute with. This paper addresses how to simplify such models while retaining their causal meaning, especially their behavior when an intervention changes part of the system.

Existing marginalization and abstraction methods can damage the causal behavior of the reduced model. The authors introduce consolidation of causal mechanisms as an alternative transformation. Its defining aim is consistent interventional behavior: simplifying the representation should preserve how the model responds to the interventions covered by the transformation.

The paper shows consolidation to be a useful method for simplifying structural causal models and discusses reductions in computational complexity. It also offers a perspective on how consolidated models might generalize. The central contribution is a way to reason about compression at the level of causal mechanisms, making intervention consistency part of the simplification objective. The discussion of generalization is presented as a perspective, rather than a blanket guarantee for every reduced model.
neurips-2023-do-not-marginalize-mechanis.tldr: Consolidating causal mechanisms simplifies structural causal models while preserving consistent interventional behavior.

paragraphs: Out-of-distribution detection asks a model to recognize inputs that differ from the data it was trained to handle. Auxiliary outlier examples can help train this ability, but collecting and cleaning them takes work. Dream-OOD addresses this problem by generating photorealistic outlier images using the supplied in-distribution data and class information.

The framework learns a text-conditioned latent space from the in-distribution data. It samples from low-likelihood regions of that space, then uses a diffusion model to decode those samples into images. This organizes outlier generation around a learned representation of the familiar data, with unusual latent samples providing the material for generated outliers.

Producing actual images makes the imagined outliers available for visual inspection and interpretation. The authors use both quantitative and qualitative studies to investigate the framework, and report that training with its generated samples can significantly improve out-of-distribution detection. The stated finding supports generated outliers as useful training material in the evaluated setting, while the visual outputs make their content more directly understandable.
neurips-2023-dream-the-impossible-outlie.tldr: Dream-OOD uses diffusion models to generate inspectable outlier images that can improve out-of-distribution detection.

paragraphs: This paper studies reinforcement learning in episodes where rewards may change adversarially and the transition model is unknown. Rewards are available through full information, and transitions have a linear mixture structure. Performance is measured by dynamic regret, which evaluates learning against a changing benchmark rather than a single fixed choice throughout training.

When the non-stationarity measure P_T is known, the authors give an algorithm with an improved dynamic-regret upper bound. The bound tracks feature dimension, episode length, number of episodes, and non-stationarity. They also establish a lower bound, showing that the algorithm has optimal dependence on the number of episodes K and on P_T, without claiming optimality in every parameter.

When P_T is unknown, the paper introduces an online ensemble with a meta-base organization. Its guarantee includes an additional term involving the expected switching number of the best base learner. This second result can be optimal in certain regimes. The two analyses distinguish the benefit of knowing how much the problem changes from the extra difficulty of adapting without that information.
neurips-2023-dynamic-regret-of-adversari.tldr: New dynamic-regret guarantees address changing adversarial rewards in linear mixture MDPs, with separate algorithms for known and unknown non-stationarity.

paragraphs: This paper explores how CLIP can provide its own supervision when labeled examples are scarce. Conventional pseudolabeling first trains on labeled data and then assigns provisional labels to unlabeled inputs. CLIP’s zero-shot ability allows those initial pseudolabels to be generated without task-specific training on labeled examples, creating another starting point for adaptation.

Using these zero-shot labels, the authors show that semi-supervised, transductive zero-shot, and unsupervised learning can be expressed through the same loss function. This shared formulation supports prompt-tuning strategies across the three settings. They investigate textual and visual prompts, including strategies that repeatedly refine pseudolabels as tuning proceeds.

On the studied image-classification tasks where CLIP has weaknesses, iterative strategies improve accuracy by 19.5 points in semi-supervised learning, 28.4 in transductive zero-shot learning, and 15.2 in unsupervised learning. The authors also observe a more equitable distribution of accuracy across classes. This contrasts with the class imbalance in performance they describe for conventional semi-supervised pseudolabeling, where classes with better provisional labels can receive disproportionate benefits.
neurips-2023-enhancing-clip-with-clip-ex.tldr: Iteratively refining CLIP’s own pseudolabels during prompt tuning improves accuracy across three limited-label learning settings.

paragraphs: Semi-supervised learning combines labeled examples with unlabeled data, often assuming both have matching feature distributions. This paper studies a broader setting where the unlabeled examples come from a mixed distribution that differs from the labeled data. A model fitted to the labeled portion can then assign incorrect pseudolabels, allowing errors to accumulate during training.

Self-Supervised Feature Adaptation, or SSFA, addresses this problem by separating pseudolabel prediction from the current model. It adds a self-supervised task that adapts the feature extractor to the unlabeled data. The aim is to make the representation better suited to that distribution before relying on it to generate provisional labels.

The authors evaluate SSFA with several learners that use pseudolabels and report significant improvements on labeled, unlabeled, and even unseen distributions. These results support feature adaptation as a broadly applicable component within the tested learning methods. The approach matters because it tackles the representation mismatch behind unreliable pseudolabels, reducing the dependence on features learned only from the available labeled examples.
neurips-2023-generalized-semi-supervised.tldr: SSFA adapts features to mismatched unlabeled data through self-supervision, improving pseudolabel-based learning in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Different trained neural networks can sometimes be joined by a straight line in parameter space while training and test losses remain almost unchanged. This phenomenon is called linear mode connectivity. The paper asks whether such connections also reveal a relationship between the internal features learned by the networks, beyond the similarity of their losses.

The authors introduce layerwise linear feature connectivity, a stronger notion in which the feature maps at every layer are linearly connected. They investigate networks connected using spawning or permutation methods and provide extensive empirical evidence across multiple settings. In these experiments, networks with linear mode connectivity also exhibit feature connectivity in nearly all layers.

This distinction between the definition and the observations matters: the proposed notion concerns every layer, while the empirical finding is qualified as nearly all layers. The paper also examines factors underlying feature connectivity and draws insights about permutation approaches. Its contribution is a feature-learning view of connected solutions, offering evidence that low-loss parameter connections are accompanied by structured relationships inside the networks.
neurips-2023-going-beyond-linear-mode-co.tldr: Networks with low-loss linear parameter connections also show linear feature connections in nearly all layers across the studied settings.

paragraphs: Generalized additive models combine individual effects in an interpretable prediction rule. Adding pairwise interactions can improve accuracy, but the number of candidate terms grows quadratically with the number of variables. This creates computational challenges and makes selecting a small, understandable collection of effects especially valuable, particularly when further structural constraints are required.

GRAND-SLAMIN provides a framework for learning these models with both sparsity and additional structural constraints through differentiable end-to-end training. The authors customize first-order gradient optimization to use sparse backpropagation, exploiting the sparsity of additive effects. The procedure supports any differentiable loss and is compatible with GPU computation.

For estimators using tree-based shape functions, the paper establishes finite-sample prediction bounds. Experiments on real-world datasets report favorable prediction performance, variable selection, and scalability relative to popular toolkits for additive models with interactions. The resulting models also remain competitive in accuracy with black-box models. Together, the findings support combining constrained interpretability with computational methods designed to benefit directly from a sparse model structure.
neurips-2023-grand-slamin-interpretable-.tldr: GRAND-SLAMIN learns sparse, structurally constrained additive models with interactions using GPU-compatible optimization.

paragraphs: Soft prompt tuning adapts a language model using learned prompt tokens, but its performance can depend strongly on how those tokens are initialized. The authors also observe that conventional methods may fail to learn enough task-relevant information in the prompts. InfoPrompt addresses both issues through an information-theoretic formulation of prompt learning.

The framework treats tuning as maximizing mutual information between prompts and other model parameters or encoded representations. It introduces two losses with complementary roles. One supports suitable initialization and helps prompt tokens learn task-relevant information; the other encourages the pretrained model’s output representation to reflect the information captured by those learned prompts.

Experiments show that InfoPrompt can converge significantly faster and outperform traditional prompt-tuning methods. The paper also provides a theoretical result showing that a gradient-descent-type algorithm can train the proposed mutual-information loss. The contribution connects what the prompts learn with how that information appears in the model’s representations, while supplying both experimental evidence and a formal basis for optimizing the objective.
neurips-2023-infoprompt-information-theo.tldr: InfoPrompt uses mutual-information objectives to improve soft-prompt initialization, task information, and convergence in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Medical image segmentation often has few annotated examples, making self-supervised pretraining useful. This paper targets a representational weakness of CNN-based approaches: their global and local features can struggle to capture long-range spatial relationships in anatomy. The proposed architecture supplements a UNet with keypoint features that carry information about relationships between distant locations.

A fusion layer augments CNN feature maps at multiple scales using an additional input that learns self-attention among localized keypoints. Pretraining operates at two levels. Global contrastive objectives regularize representations from the UNet bottleneck and aggregated multiscale keypoints. Locally, a distance-based rule establishes keypoint correspondences and encourages the matched features to be similar.

MRI and CT experiments separate the architectural contribution from the pretraining contribution. With random initialization across architectures, the proposed design shows advantages over CNN- and Transformer-based UNets. Adding the proposed pretraining further improves performance over existing self-supervised methods, producing more robust self-attention and reported state-of-the-art segmentation results. These findings support combining local CNN features with longer-range keypoint relationships when annotations are limited.
neurips-2023-keypoint-augmented-self-sup.tldr: Multiscale keypoint attention and global-local self-supervised pretraining improve medical segmentation with limited annotations.

paragraphs: An affordance describes how an object can support an action, and point-level affordances can guide robotic manipulation. This paper studies articulated objects in environments where occlusions and physical constraints affect what actions are possible. It argues that object-centered predictions alone overlook relevant surroundings and differences in the physical form of the acting agent.

The proposed framework combines object-level actionable information with environmental constraints. Learning this directly is difficult because occluders can vary in number, geometry, position, and pose, producing many possible combinations. To address that growth in scene complexity, the authors introduce contrastive affordance learning designed to use training data more efficiently.

The framework can train on scenes with a single occluder and generalize to scenes containing more complex occluder combinations. Experiments demonstrate its effectiveness at learning affordances that account for environmental constraints. The main significance is that action suitability is learned in relation to the surrounding scene, while the training design reduces the need to represent every combination of occlusions explicitly in the training scenes.
neurips-2023-learning-environment-aware-.tldr: Contrastive affordance learning uses single-occluder training scenes to support manipulation predictions under more complex occlusions.

paragraphs: This paper studies local convergence of gradient dynamics in differentiable two-player zero-sum games. Near an equilibrium, the relevant Jacobian separates into a symmetric component S and an antisymmetric component A. Earlier continuous-time results establish local convergence when S is positive definite, while dynamics may diverge when S is zero.

The authors show that partial curvature can suffice: S may be merely nonzero and positive semidefinite, provided the eigenvectors of A are in general position relative to the kernel of S. They also analyze cases where S is small compared with A. There, the convergence rate typically depends on the average eigenvalue of S, rather than its smallest eigenvalue.

An application considers computing mixed Nash equilibria in continuous games. Methods that optimize both the weights and locations of strategy particles generically converge faster than methods with fixed locations, thanks to partial curvature. The result gives a conditional explanation for why adding degrees of freedom can help: those extra freedoms can introduce curvature that improves local game dynamics.
neurips-2023-local-convergence-of-gradie.tldr: Partial curvature suffices for local convergence of continuous-time game dynamics under a general-position condition.

paragraphs: Zero-shot neural architecture search ranks candidate networks without training each one. Existing scoring proxies can still require backpropagation or depend strongly on the chosen data and labels. This paper develops MeCo, a proxy based on the minimum eigenvalue of feature-map correlation, requiring a single forward pass with one random input.

The method is motivated by an analysis connecting the Pearson correlation matrix of feature maps to convergence rate and generalization capacity in overparameterized networks. The authors also propose MeCo_opt to improve the approach. Their evaluations examine how well the proxy’s rankings correlate with actual architecture performance across several benchmarks.

MeCo achieves the highest reported correlation among the compared proxies, including 0.89 on NATS-Bench-TSS with CIFAR-10, while being independent of data and labels. Integrated into an existing architecture-generation method, it also supports low-cost search. One reported searched network reaches 97.31% accuracy on CIFAR-10, 0.04 percentage points above the baselines under the same settings. These results connect an inexpensive structural score with useful architecture selection in the tested searches.
neurips-2023-meco-zero-shot-nas-with-one.tldr: MeCo ranks untrained architectures using feature correlations from one random input and one forward pass.

paragraphs: Self-supervised learning can produce representations that reflect meaningful structure without explicit labels, yet its many loss functions can seem disconnected or heuristic. This paper develops a theoretical perspective intended to explain how such methods work. It focuses on the role of data augmentation in shaping what a learned representation is encouraged to preserve.

The authors view the problem through a Laplace operator and connect the inductive bias introduced by augmentation to low-rank matrix completion. This creates a bridge between spectral embedding and the problem of recovering a low-rank matrix. Rather than treating augmentation only as a training procedure, the analysis treats it as a source of mathematical structure in the learning problem.

Using results from low-rank matrix completion, the paper analyzes convergence of modern self-supervised methods and a key property affecting their downstream performance. The contribution is an explanatory framework linking augmentation, representation learning, and existing theory. It provides a way to investigate why the learning process converges and what influences the usefulness of the resulting features for later tasks.
neurips-2023-neural-harmonics-bridging-s.tldr: A Laplace-operator perspective connects augmentation-driven self-supervised learning to low-rank matrix completion and its theoretical guarantees.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning uses historical data to learn sequential decisions. This paper asks what makes that learning sample-efficient when value functions are approximated. It introduces a notion of data diversity that includes earlier coverage measures, giving a shared way to describe how the available dataset supports learning.

The authors use this notion to analyze three algorithm families: version-space methods, regularized optimization, and posterior sampling. Under standard assumptions, all three achieve comparable sample efficiency. Their analysis recovers state-of-the-art suboptimality bounds for finite and linear model classes, bringing these approaches into a common theoretical comparison.

The result revises a picture in which regularized optimization appeared to require more samples than version-space methods. It also establishes a role for posterior sampling, which has received less attention offline because of its association with exploration. The paper introduces a new model-free posterior-sampling algorithm with frequentist, worst-case suboptimality bounds. The contribution is both a unifying account of data requirements and an algorithmic alternative supported by that account.
neurips-2023-on-sample-efficient-offline.tldr: A unified data-diversity framework gives comparable sample-efficiency guarantees for three offline RL algorithm families under standard assumptions.

paragraphs: Synthetic time series are useful for expanding datasets, representing rare events, and constructing counterfactual scenarios. Such sequences may need both realistic statistical behavior and compliance with numerical constraints. This paper addresses that combination, which arises in applications such as financial stress scenarios and energy data.

Existing approaches can encode constraints through training penalties and discard samples that violate them. Changing constraints may then require retraining, while rejecting many samples can become costly or impractical. The authors formulate generation as constrained optimization and develop several generative methods, including the guided diffusion model GuidedDiffTime, to support efficient sampling while maintaining realism.

Evaluations on financial and energy datasets show qualitative and quantitative improvements over existing work. GuidedDiffTime also accommodates new constraints without retraining, which the authors associate with a carbon-footprint reduction of up to 92% relative to existing deep learning methods. This is a reported maximum from the evaluated comparisons. The practical contribution is a generation approach that can respond to changing scenario requirements without repeatedly rebuilding the model.
neurips-2023-on-the-constrained-time-ser.tldr: GuidedDiffTime generates realistic constrained time series and supports new constraints without retraining.

paragraphs: Dataset distillation seeks a small synthetic dataset that retains the predictive value of a much larger one. This paper studies theoretical questions behind that compression: how small the distilled set can be and how much prediction risk it adds. The analysis focuses on kernel ridge regression with shift-invariant kernels.

The authors reformulate ridge regression in a random Fourier feature space. They prove that a small set of instances exists in the original input space whose solution in that feature space matches the full dataset’s solution. Using those instances for kernel ridge regression then gives an approximation to the solution obtained from the complete data.

The required set size is linear in the random-feature dimension, or alternatively nearly linear in the effective degrees of freedom. Those degrees of freedom depend on the kernel, dataset size, and regularization parameter; the error bound also depends on regularization. Analytical and empirical checks support the bounds. The result distinguishes exact agreement in the random-feature formulation from approximation of the full kernel solution, providing explicit theoretical structure for the compression tradeoff.
neurips-2023-on-the-size-and-approximati.tldr: For shift-invariant kernels, the paper proves small distilled datasets exist and bounds their size and approximation error.

paragraphs: ResMem investigates whether explicit memorization can improve generalization beyond an existing prediction model. Its starting point is the model’s residuals: the differences between its predictions and the training labels. These remaining errors become a second learning target, allowing a separate component to capture information the original predictor has not fitted.

The method fits a nearest-neighbor-based regressor to those residuals. At prediction time, its output is added to the original model’s prediction. This construction can explicitly memorize training labels, while retaining the original model as part of the final predictor. The approach therefore combines a learned prediction with a correction derived from stored training information.

The authors first analyze a stylized linear regression problem and prove more favorable test risk than a base linear neural network. They then report consistent test-set improvements across standard vision and natural-language-processing benchmarks. The theoretical guarantee belongs to the stylized setting, while the broader evidence is empirical. Together, these results show that explicit residual memorization can improve predictions on unseen examples in the studied problems.
neurips-2023-resmem-learn-what-you-can-a.tldr: ResMem adds a nearest-neighbor residual predictor to an existing model, improving generalization in theory and the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Neural text-processing systems need a way to convert words into numerical representations. RETVec is a multilingual vectorizer designed to make that conversion efficient and resilient to altered text. Its focus includes ordinary typing mistakes and character-level adversarial changes, both of which can make a word look different at the input.

The vectorizer combines a new character encoding with an optional small embedding model to represent words in a 256-dimensional space. The embedding model is pretrained using pairwise metric learning to build resistance to typos and adversarial character changes. This puts robustness into the representation stage that supplies inputs to the text-processing model.

The authors compare RETVec with leading vectorizers and word embeddings across popular architectures and datasets. They report competitive multilingual models with significantly stronger resilience to the evaluated typos and adversarial text attacks. The result supports the input vectorizer as a useful place to improve robustness while maintaining competitive task performance. RETVec is also released under the Apache 2 license, making the proposed component available for use.
neurips-2023-retvec-resilient-and-effici.tldr: RETVec produces efficient multilingual word representations that improve resilience to typos and character-level attacks in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: This paper revisits multilayer perceptrons as image-learning models. Because MLPs lack vision-specific inductive biases, they offer a direct test of how far scale can compensate for missing architectural guidance. They also matter for theory: researchers frequently analyze MLPs as stand-ins for more complex networks, despite limited large-pretraining evidence about their behavior.

The authors find that MLP performance improves substantially with scale, reporting 95% on CIFAR10, 82% on CIFAR100, and 58% on ImageNet ReaL. These results demonstrate that scaling can compensate for the absence of vision-specific bias in the studied settings. They provide empirical reference points for assessing claims about the relationship between architecture and scale.

MLPs also largely reproduce the behavior of modern architectures, although some components of the learning setup have stronger or unexpected effects. This supports their usefulness as theoretical proxies while identifying differences that deserve attention. All experiments ran on a single GPU, and the authors emphasize that MLP computational efficiency can make large-pretraining studies more accessible to academic researchers.
neurips-2023-scaling-mlps-a-tale-of-indu.tldr: Scaled MLPs improve substantially on vision tasks and broadly mirror modern networks, providing evidence about inductive bias and theoretical proxies.

paragraphs: Neuro-symbolic systems need operations that connect logical reasoning with neural representations. Soft-unification makes one such connection by replacing symbolic term comparison with comparison in an embedding space. This allows logical rule learning to become differentiable, so the comparison mechanism can participate in end-to-end training.

The paper examines what properties soft-unification should have. These include avoiding redundancy within proofs, assigning well-defined scores to proofs, and providing non-sparse gradients for learning. The authors argue that earlier systems, including the Neural Theorem Prover, do not satisfy these properties, motivating a different foundation for the operation.

Their framework, DeepSoftLog, uses probabilistic semantics in place of fuzzy semantics. Experiments show that it can outperform state-of-the-art methods on neuro-symbolic benchmarks, supporting the usefulness of the proposed properties. The contribution goes beyond making symbolic matching approximate: it examines how approximate matching interacts with proof structure, scoring, and optimization. The empirical claim is that this more principled formulation can improve performance, rather than that it wins universally.
neurips-2023-soft-unification-in-deep-pr.tldr: DeepSoftLog gives soft-unification a probabilistic foundation to improve proof behavior and learning in neuro-symbolic systems.

paragraphs: Fine-grained representation learning can benefit from relationships that emerge between local image views and the image as a whole. Those relational representations can be difficult to interpret. This paper aims to express them as understandable graphs over image views, making the relationships used by the model more explicit.

The authors first show theoretically that the abstract relational representations recover transitive relationships among local views. They use this result to design Transitivity Recovering Decompositions, or TRD, a search algorithm operating in graph space. TRD identifies interpretable equivalents of the emergent relationships at both the individual-instance and class levels, without requiring separate post-hoc computations.

The paper also proves robustness to noisy views and provides empirical evidence supporting that result. In the reported evaluations, TRD matches or exceeds state-of-the-art performance while remaining fully interpretable. The significance is that the graph representation serves as part of the relationship-learning approach itself, and its robustness helps preserve predictive performance when some views are noisy. The work links an explanatory decomposition with both theoretical and empirical support.
neurips-2023-transitivity-recovering-dec.tldr: TRD expresses fine-grained image relationships as interpretable graphs and provides theoretical and empirical robustness to noisy views.
